title: A Playlist for the Tryouts
premise: August Marchetti transferred to Hollow Creek High mid-junior year carrying a secret: his family fled a scandal in his old town, and the truth could still destroy them. When English teacher Ms. Okafor assigns a college essay on 'the one honest thing you've never said,' August writes about the night everything fell apart—then panics and shreds it. But his best friend Dev reads the fragments in the recycling bin, and the school's beloved choir director begins building the spring showcase around anonymous student confessions set to music. As the audition deadline looms, August must choose between confessing publicly and protecting Dev's trust, since Dev's own family was hurt by the same scandal. In the end, August performs the song himself at the final audition, names what he did, and loses Dev's friendship for a season—but wins back something harder: a self he doesn't have to hide.
about_author: Rafael Pemberton is a former high school debate coach who spent six years listening to teenagers say true things by accident. He writes from a small apartment above a record shop, where the neighbors' bass line sets his pacing.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: August's POV. Three months into Hollow Creek High, August has perfected invisibility: safe seat, safe answers, safe silence. He catalogs the rules of not being known while dodging Dev's invitations to actually hang out. Emotional beat: the loneliness of safety, established through small evasions that read as politeness.

chapters.title: The Question Nobody Can Stop Answering
chapters.summary: August's POV. Ms. Okafor posts the college essay prompt—an honest thing you've never said—and the classroom hums with half-confessions. That night August writes four pages about the scandal back home, then shreds them at 2 a.m. Emotional beat: the terrifying relief of writing truth, immediately followed by panic.

chapters.title: Recycling Bin Archaeology
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev, curious and loyal to a fault, retrieves the shredded pages for a journalism project on 'found texts' and pieces enough together to recognize August's handwriting—and a name Dev knows all too well. Emotional beat: betrayal discovered secondhand; Dev says nothing but starts watching August differently.

chapters.title: Something Old Under the Gym
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The school announces the spring showcase: anonymous student confessions set to music by the choir. Meanwhile maintenance crews find sealed rooms beneath the gym, and rumors fly that the school itself is built over buried history—a mirror August can't ignore. Emotional beat: dread turning into inevitability.

chapters.title: Locker Shut, Door Open
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev confronts August obliquely, leaving an anonymous note in his locker quoting his own shredded essay back at him. August realizes someone knows, and suspects everyone. Their friendship curdles into polite performance. Emotional beat: paranoia; the cost of secrets compounding daily.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Track
chapters.summary: August's POV. A confession song appears in the showcase auditions—clearly built from August's words, submitted under no name. The whole school speculates; Ms. Okafor asks August directly if he recognizes the voice of it. He lies to her face. Emotional beat: shame sharpening into resolve to reclaim his own story.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Kind of Lie
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev admits to himself he submitted the track—not to expose August, but because hearing the truth sung felt like justice for his own family. Torn between loyalty and truth, Dev gives August until the final audition to come forward voluntarily. Emotional beat: grief for a friendship both boys are still pretending exists.

chapters.title: What Survival Cost
chapters.summary: August's POV. August visits his mother, who begs him to stay silent a little longer—the legal dust hasn't settled. He sees, finally, that her survival plan requires him to stay a ghost forever. Emotional beat: the quiet horror of realizing protection and erasure look identical.

chapters.title: Final Auditions
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Audition day. Dev waits to see if August will speak; August walks onstage uninvited, takes the mic, and performs the confession himself—naming the scandal, his part in it, and Dev's family by apology. The room goes silent, then Ms. Okafor simply says, 'Thank you for telling the truth.' Emotional beat: climax—public truth, total exposure, no net.

chapters.title: A Playlist for What Comes Next
chapters.summary: August's POV, weeks later. Consequences land: some classmates turn away, others thank him quietly; his mother is furious, then, slowly, relieved. Dev doesn't forgive him yet, but leaves a burned CD in August's locker—track one blank, track two titled 'maybe.' August submits the real essay, unshredded. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—truth didn't fix everything, but it made him real.
